description: The northstar says runtime modules warm lazily and the root should pull only reached runtime surfaces. In the Enum.reduce operator-ref survey, DefineModule publishes FunctionSource x217 changed facts for whole runtime modules, while only a small subset is later expanded/defined/lowered/analyzed. Current source_publish::publish_scope reserves/publishes every function in a demanded module because ModuleInterface and FunctionSource are coupled at module-definition granularity. This is not semantic closure overreach, but it is still spreadsheet-model overproduction: cells unrelated to the demand become facts and can churn readers/waiters. Strategy: research a split surface contract: module interface/export facts can be produced without publishing all FunctionSource facts, then exact callable demand publishes FunctionSource(function) for the requested callable. Preserve source-order macro semantics and diagnostics; runtime bootstrap may need pre-indexed callable source spans or per-callable source thunks. Signal: for fixtures2/00181_enum_reduce_operator_ref.fz, cold runtime functions should remain without FunctionSource facts unless needed for interface/export proof.

comments.text: fz-go4.18.12 audit re-confirmed with counts at 014aa505f: FunctionSource facts stashed vs functions actually expanded = 224 vs 13 (00181), 72/13 (00001), 67/5 (00026), 66/7 (escaped_callable). The cold-overproduction magnitude is ~5-17x.

title: Compiler2 runtime module definition should not publish cold function-source facts
